models.notes: Also uses videos/extensions for clip continue. Fresh text/image-to-video allows 1-15s; the new portion of a reference/continue call is tighter (often <=10s, not independently confirmed to the second — maxExtensionSeconds is a conservative estimate, not a documented exact figure). 1080p pricing (0.25/s) may actually belong to a separate 'Grok Imagine 1.5' variant not yet split out as its own catalog entry — base model 480p/720p rates (0.05/0.07) are confirmed against docs.x.ai. aspect_ratio/resolution are NOT accepted on videos/extensions -- the extension output always matches the source clip's aspect ratio (docs.x.ai).
models.pricingNotes: Video $/sec by resolution from product catalog (verify docs.x.ai/developers pricing). As of 2026-08 xAI publishes generation pricing, not a separate ref-image or extend line item (docs.x.ai video + pricing). videoReferenceImageCost=0 means no separate ref fee. videoExtendCostPerSecond uses same billing unit as generation new seconds; set to 0.07 (720p catalog rate) for planning when resolution-specific extend rates are not published.

models.notes: Prompt-based edit of an already-generated clip via POST videos/edits: takes an existing video + a text instruction, returns a new video. Output always inherits the source clip's duration and resolution (not independently configurable) and input is capped at 8.7s by xAI. video can be a Files API file_id or a url/data URI; this app tries a stored file_id (from generation-time storage_options) first and falls back to a base64 data URI of the local clip file on any failure.
models.pricingNotes: xAI has not published edit-specific pricing as of 2026-08. videoCostPerSecondByResolution is proxied from grok-imagine-video's own generation rate (same provider/model family) as a labeled estimate, not confirmed edit pricing — verify against docs.x.ai before relying on this for cost reporting.

models.notes: Open-weights 13B DiT video generation model hosted on Fal.ai serverless GPUs. Billed as a flat ~$0.40/video (frame-count-based generation, not duration-based) — NOT per-second; a prior per-second rate here (0.005/s) underpriced a 5s clip by ~16x ($0.025 vs the real ~$0.40 flat fee). Single init/reference image only (true i2v) — not Grok-style multi-plate identity conditioning; attaching more than one is misleading. Deliberately no min/max/absMaxClipDurationSeconds: the real API parameter is num_frames (85 or 129) + fps, not seconds — forcing a seconds-shaped min/max onto a frame-count model would itself be a wrong approximation; now represented directly via shortClipFrameCount/longClipFrameCount (the model's real NumberofFramesEnum: 85 or 129, default 129) rather than a generic duration bound. numInferenceSteps default 30 confirmed against fal.ai/models/fal-ai/hunyuan-video/api. Supports 16:9 or 9:16 aspect ratio (fal.ai/models/fal-ai/hunyuan-video/api).
models.pricingNotes: Update from vendor pricing page when rates change; Engine has no USD fallbacks.

models.notes: Alibaba Wan 2.1 open-weights image-to-video model hosted on Fal.ai serverless GPUs. Billed as a flat fee per video (frame-count-based generation, not duration-based), not per-second — a prior per-second rate here (0.025/s) underpriced a 5s 720p clip by ~3x ($0.125 vs the real ~$0.40 flat fee). 1080p flat fee not independently documented; assumed equal to 720p pending confirmation. Duration is a narrow ~5-6s band (81-100 frames @ 5-24fps typical), NOT the generic 3-10s range — approximated here in seconds even though frames+fps is the more precise real parameter. Single init/reference image only (true i2v) — not Grok-style multi-plate identity conditioning; attaching more than one is misleading. numInferenceSteps default 30 confirmed against fal.ai/models/fal-ai/wan-i2v/api. Deliberately no shortClipFrameCount/longClipFrameCount: Wan's real num_frames (default 81, range 81-100 per fal-ai/wan-i2v) is a continuous range, not Hunyuan's discrete short/long enum, and FalVideoClient does not send an explicit num_frames override for Wan today — this entry stays duration-native via min/max/absMaxClipDurationSeconds above instead. "auto" (default) infers aspect ratio from the input image (fal.ai/models/fal-ai/wan-i2v/api).
models.pricingNotes: Flat base $/video from fal.ai wan pricing pages (per generation). per-sec=0. Refs are the single init image included in generation price → videoReferenceImageCost=0. No continue → no extend rate.

models.notes: Wired via GeminiVideoClient (text/image-to-video only). Documented duration is exactly 4, 6, or 8 seconds (not an arbitrary range) — 1080p/4K surfaces often restrict to 8s only; no 480p support. Some surfaces document up to 3 multi-image 'ingredients' reference images, but GeminiVideoClient does not implement that conditioning path — it throws NotSupportedException rather than silently ignoring reference images, so maxReferenceImages is 0 here (fail loud) until ingredients support is actually built. Confirmed via Gemini video docs / AI Studio Veo / Cloud Veo 3.1 pages, not yet verified against a live account. ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/veo: landscape 16:9 (default) or portrait 9:16.
models.pricingNotes: Vertex/Gemini Veo published $/sec class rates in catalog; confirm cloud.google.com Veo pricing. Ref images: no separate published add-on in our matrix → 0. No continue → no extend rate.

models.notes: xAI's actual latest generation, newer than grok-4.5 despite the lower-looking version number (4.20 > 4.5 as sequential minor releases, not decimals) — discovered via direct xAI model-list API call, not previously in this catalog. Its own aliases tag it beta/experimental (grok-4.20-beta, grok-4.20-experimental-beta-...), so treat results with more caution than the established grok-4/grok-4.5. Confirmed live: accepts temperature normally, but REJECTS reasoning_effort outright ("does not support parameter reasoningEffort", camelCase/no-underscore in the error text — GrokChatClient's self-heal matches both spellings) — it appears to always reason without an exposed effort dial. context_length confirmed 1,000,000 via API; pricing is an unverified placeholder copied from grok-4 (xAI's own price fields use an internal unit not yet decoded to $/M). maxOutputTokens=128000 confirmed via docs.x.ai/developers/rest-api-reference/inference/chat: max_completion_tokens defaults to 128,000 when unset platform-wide (per max_completion_tokens's own definition this excludes reasoning tokens, so this is the visible-JSON-output ceiling even for the reasoning variant — not a per-model published figure).

Model: Suno v5.5. Provider: Suno API (sunoapi.org) — unofficial reseller. Documented duration 10-360s on V5_5 custom mode.
Model: Suno. Provider: AI Music API (aimusicapi.ai) — different unofficial reseller. No documented duration control; client mix trims to scene length.

ElevenLabs 'Eleven Music' (POST /v1/music, model music_v2). Uses the same ElevenLabs_API_KEY as narrator voice — no separate Suno reseller account. 3s–10min; instrumental by default, can sing. Streams audio bytes (served via data: URL through the media proxy).
Spoken dialogue from a personal clone sample on Cast.

Creates a voice profile from a short mic/upload sample (Cast → Voice clone sample). Optional paid add-on path. Requires an ElevenLabs API key with Instant Voice Cloning permission (create_instant_voice_clone). Keys without that scope return 401 missing_permissions — switch to fal-ai/minimax/voice-clone or upgrade the key.

Clones a voice from a reference sample (>=10s, reuses this project's existing assets/characters/{key}/voice_clone_sample.* upload) via Fal.ai's queue API (fal.ai/models/fal-ai/minimax/voice-clone). Input: audio_url (URL or data URI). Output: custom_voice_id, reused across many fal-ai/minimax/speech-02-hd calls so the clone cost is paid once. $1.50 per clone call — confirmed via fal.ai's own model/pricing page and openapi schema (2026-08). A preview-text option exists ($0.30/1000 chars) but this app's client never requests it. MiniMax retains the cloned voice only if used by a speech call at least once within 7 days of creation (provider-side retention, not enforced by this app).

Text-to-speech via Fal.ai's queue API (fal.ai/models/fal-ai/minimax/speech-02-hd) using a voice cloned by fal-ai/minimax/voice-clone (custom_voice_id passed as voice_setting.voice_id — confirmed against MiniMax's own platform.minimax.io voice-cloning docs, same convention). Input: text (max 5000 chars per call, this app does not auto-chunk longer narration), voice_setting {voice_id, speed 0.5-2.0, vol, pitch, emotion}. Output: audio.url + duration_ms. $0.10 per 1000 characters — confirmed via fal.ai's own model/pricing page (2026-08).

Sync Labs Lipsync 2 Pro via Fal.ai's queue API (fal.ai/models/fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v2/pro). Input: video_url, audio_url (both URL or data URI), optional sync_mode (cut_off default | loop | bounce | silence | remap) for when the two durations differ. Output: video.url. Zero-shot — no fine-tuning needed; preserves natural teeth/facial detail per Fal's own listing. ~$5/min of output video (~$0.083/s) — sourced via targeted search during research (fal.ai's own pricing page returned HTTP 429 rate-limiting when fetched directly; cross-checked against Sync Labs' own sync.so/pricing page, which lists the same figure for their Pro tier). Confirm against fal.ai's live pricing page before relying on this for a large narration/dub run.

Newest Sync Labs model on Fal.ai (fal.ai/models/fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v3), same core video_url/audio_url/sync_mode input as v2 Pro plus an optional `options` object (model_mode: lips/face/head/lipsync/emotion/talking_head, prompt: emotion tag, temperature, active_speaker_detection, occlusion_detection_enabled) that this app's client does not yet expose. Pricing not confirmed — fal.ai's pricing page returned HTTP 429 during research and no third-party source for v3 specifically was found; left null rather than guessed. Not the capability default until pricing is confirmed.
